name: Shifa Medical Store
story:
Written in 1998 by a two-person software house for a family pharmacy in Satellite Town.
It printed every bill and kept the stock until the software house closed in 2004.
The shop still runs it every day. Nobody has the source code.

knownRules.text: GST is 17% of the bill after discount, truncated (not rounded) to the paisa.
A bill whose subtotal is over Rs 5,000 gets 10% off, truncated. Exactly Rs 5,000 gets no discount. The discount comes before GST.
A medicine whose batch has expired cannot be added to a bill. A batch that expires today can.
Saving a bill takes the quantity of each item off that medicine's stock.
Bill numbers are YYMM-#### from the bill date, counting from 0001 again each month.
A quantity larger than the stock is refused when the item is added.
A new customer gets the next id (C0009 after C0008), and a blank name is refused.

knownBugs.text: The expiry check compares two-digit years. In 1998 it blocks batches good until 2000; from 2000 it sells batches that expired in the 1990s.
A quantity of 0 skips the stock check, and editing the line (F3) never checks again, so a bill can take stock below zero.

The 10% discount is worked out as subtotal x 10 in a 32-bit number, which wraps around above Rs 21,47,483.64. A bill for 9,999 insulin (qty 0, then F3) gets a negative discount and saves at Rs 78,48,837.88 instead of Rs 68,43,815.55.
